paper.title_en: Joint constraints on quantum Oppenheimer–Snyder black holes from high-frequency quasi-periodic oscillations in X-ray binary systems and the S2 star orbit
paper.abstract_en: We study a quantum-corrected version of the Oppenheimer–Snyder (OS) spacetime in which classical collapse is modified by a single effective parameter α, representing small quantum gravitational effects in a phenomenologically rescaled form. Although the correction enters through a term proportional to αM<sup loc="post">2</sup>/r<sup loc="post">4</sup>, it produces noticeable changes in the strong-field region while leaving weak-field physics almost unchanged. One of the main results is the appearance of a minimum mass for horizon formation, <math altimg="si19.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo linebreak="badbreak">−</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.16em"/><msub><mi>M</mi><mo>⊙</mo></msub></mrow></math> for the effective parameter α ≈ 0.22. We emphasize that this Mmin is expressed in terms of the effective parameter α; in terms of the bare loop quantum gravity (LQG) parameter, <math altimg="si20.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mtext>Pl</mtext></msub><mo>∼</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> g, consistent with the theoretical expectation. Orbital properties are also slightly modified, with the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) shifting to <math altimg="si21.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>O</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>M</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mi>α</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, giving corrections of order <math altimg="si22.svg"><mrow><mo>∼</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> for stellar black holes and <math altimg="si23.svg"><mrow><mo>∼</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> for Sgr A*. In the same region, radial epicyclic frequencies change by about <math altimg="si24.svg"><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></math> near r ∼ 5M, while vertical modes are less affected, leading to small but structured shifts in quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) behavior. Using four X-ray binaries (GRS 1915+105, XTE J1550-564, XTE J1859+226, GRO J1655-40), we find a consistent range <math altimg="si18.svg"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0.22</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.10</mn></mrow></math>, with masses between <math altimg="si25.svg"><mrow><mn>5.4</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mn>12.4</mn><mspace width="0.16em"/><msub><mi>M</mi><mo>⊙</mo></msub></mrow></math> and emission radii <math altimg="si26.svg"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>∼</mo><mn>5.5</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mn>8.6</mn></mrow></math>. The observed QPO frequencies, lying in the range <math altimg="si27.svg"><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mn>450</mn></mrow></math> Hz, are well reproduced within this framework. Weak-field tests such as S2 and Mercury still allow <math altimg="si28.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>1.10</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.19</mn></mrow></math>, leaving room for these small strong-gravity corrections. This work demonstrates that while bare Planck-scale corrections are unobservable, effective rescaled parameters that encode the collective effect of quantum gravity can be constrained by current astrophysical observations.
